subtitle: What happens when decision intelligence gets dramatically cheaper — and which engineering disciplines become mandatory.

takeaways: Cheaper decisions increase demand for decisions.
Governance and evaluation become core product surfaces.

body.text: Why this matters

TypeSafe explicitly invokes Jevons’ paradox: cheaper intelligence may increase consumption. If decision calls become nearly free, software will sprout millions of micro-judgements — monitoring, ranking, gating, triage — that were previously uneconomic.
What cheaper intelligence unlocks
What still breaks
Conclusion
The future of automation belongs to teams who instrument decisions. Models are necessary; measurement is decisive.

Forward-looking scenario planning should include failure modes: provider outages, sudden price changes, regulatory constraints on automated decisions, and user trust collapses after a single high-impact false negative. Build kill switches. Prefer progressive delivery of automation — suggest, then shadow, then enforce. Connect Insights research to Jobs and Teams pages so organisational capability grows with technical capability. The most durable advantage is not access to a single model API; it is a culture that can swap models without rewriting the business.
